Specimen: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for suspected Fragile X syndrome

METHODOLOGY
PCR-based assay for detection of CGG repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene (FRAXA locus). This assay detects normal, intermediate, premutation, and full mutation size ranges. DNA was extracted from peripheral blood and analyzed using fluorescent PCR with capillary electrophoresis for accurate sizing of CGG repeats.

Technical Note: Normal alleles contain 5-44 CGG repeats, intermediate alleles 45-54 repeats, premutation alleles 55-200 repeats, and full mutations >200 repeats.

RESULTS
FMR1 Gene Analysis:
Allele 1: 30 CGG repeats (Normal)
Allele 2: 29 CGG repeats (Normal)

No expansion mutations detected in the FMR1 gene.

SUMMARY
Normal results. The patient has two normal-sized FMR1 alleles with no evidence of CGG repeat expansion. Based on these findings, Fragile X syndrome is very unlikely. It should be noted that a small proportion (<1%) of Fragile X cases may be caused by point mutations or other rearrangements within the FMR1 gene that are not detected by this PCR-based expansion analysis.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
